body:
The "incremental state-observation cursor" is the StateChangeFeed cursor of the pinned @ordarium v1.3.1 (pin == pnpm-workspace overrides == installed package.json). It is exposed as StateChangePage.cursor from changes(filter?, cursor?) (core StateStore.changes; implemented by core MemoryLedger and by @ordarium/ledger-sqlite SqliteLedger, the crash-durable one used here), capability-gated on capabilities.stateChangeFeed + supportsStateChangeFeed, else LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED.

EXACT SEMANTICS
- Type: { changes: StateRecord[]; cursor: string; hasMore: boolean }. cursor is ALWAYS present, even on an empty page (unlike the optional nextCursor? of the other read surfaces); with no input cursor an empty feed yields {"c":"0"}.
- Encoding: opaque base64url of UTF-8 JSON {"c":"<decimal>"}; decode requires a non-null non-array object, c a ^[0-9]+$ string, and Number(c) a non-negative safe integer; anything else throws InvalidCursorError (code INVALID_CURSOR), distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT. Not signed/authenticated.
- Meaning: c is the global state-change position (SQLite ordarium_state_changes.change_seq, INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT; contiguous 1..n in MemoryLedger) of the LAST DELIVERED change. Not "next to read", not a per-subject revision, not a timestamp, not an event id.
- Resume is strictly-after and ascending: a call with cursor P returns only changes with position > P, so the change at P is never re-delivered. Absent cursor => after = 0 => from the beginning.
- Filter-independent: the position is in the global all-namespace commit order; filter.namespace only narrows which records are returned, so the same cursor is valid with a different/absent filter. Caveat: it advances only to the last matching delivered change, so a namespace filter never skips the cursor forward over other namespaces' commits.
- Page size: filter.limit defaults to 100 and must be a safe integer in [1,1000] (RESOURCE_LIMITS.maxStateChangePageItems) else TypeError; fetch is LIMIT bound+1; hasMore is true iff at least one further MATCHING change already exists beyond the page.
- Atomicity/durability: the ordering row is inserted in the same transaction as the revision insert in compareAndSetState, so a committed revision and its observable position cannot split, and a rolled-back CAS leaves neither; positions are monotone and never reused. Migration v3->v4 backfills deterministic synthetic positions in (namespace,key,revision) order, labelled migration order rather than original commit order.
- Fail-closed validation: a decoded position greater than the global high-water mark (SELECT MAX(change_seq), COALESCE 0) throws InvalidCursorError; a dangling ordering row (LEFT-JOIN miss) throws LedgerCorruptError.

THE DECISION ENCODED (ORD-BOOT-0 / -0.1): opaque cursor (no position-guessing, encoding can evolve); global filter-independent position (portable across filters, single validation mark); always-present durable resume position rather than finite pagination; exclusive resume (duplicate-free polling); fail-closed INVALID_CURSOR kept distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT because concurrent commits only raise the mark (a valid cursor cannot be falsely rejected) while a restored/replaced ledger lowers it and restarting from 0 would duplicate; explicit capability declaration; atomic position assignment; honest synthetic backfill for pre-v4 history.

DISAMBIGUATION: listStates uses a different keyset-pagination cursor (nextCursor?, {"s":"<namespace>\0<key>"}) over current subjects, not commit order - this is what src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts pages. The workspace's own graph.project.cursor (=MAX(event_id)) and viewCursor (v1:<epoch>:<eventCursor>:<viewGeneration>) are unrelated. The workspace does not consume the change feed at all (0 references in src).

PROVENANCE: authoritative source is the pinned artifact; no lockfile, but pin/overrides/installed agree on 1.3.1. docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md still logs a 1.2.0 baseline, but it is a dated revision log superseded by the 1.3.1 pins and does not address this cursor, so it is not co-applicable and no peer escalation is warranted.
